The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate ${lim}_{x\to \,\,-2}f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
As $x$ approaches $-2$ from the right, the function value $f(x)$ grows to infinity, and therefore

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{2}^{+}}f(x)=\infty .
$$

However, as $x$ approaches $-2$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ goes to $-\infty $, and therefore

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{2}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty .
$$

Consequently, 

$$
{lim}_{x\to -2}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate ${lim}_{x\to \,5}f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
As $x$ approaches $5$ from the left, the function value $f(x)$ goes to $-\infty $, and therefore

$$
{lim}_{x\to {5}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty .
$$

However, the function is not defined for $x>5,$ and consequently, we cannot approach $x=5$ from the right. So we have 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {5}^{+}}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

Therefore, 
  

$$
{lim}_{x\to 5}f(x)=\text{DNE}.
$$

The figure above shows the graph of $f(x).$ Evaluate ${lim}_{x\to \,-1}f(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
We see from the graph that as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the left, the function $f(x)$ approaches $-\infty .$ So, the left-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{-}}f(x)=-\infty \,.
$$

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the right, the function $f(x)$ again approaches $-\infty .$ So, the right-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{x\to (-1)^{+}}f(x)=-\infty \,.
$$

Consequently,

$$
{lim}_{x\to -1}f(x)=-\infty \,.
$$
